transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I suppose I should start by saying that I didn't just wake up one morning and decide to come here. It's been building up, you see. It's my in-laws. We've always had our disagreements, like any family, I suppose. You know how it is, the little bickering at Thanksgiving, the snide comments about my potato salad... but this, this is different. It's not just arguing anymore. I finally realized, and it all became so clear to me the other day when I was looking at the church bulletin, that they are actually using the altar—the very altar where I was married, mind you—and the entire parish committee to completely push me out. They want to erase me. They are actively plotting to make everyone in the congregation, and everyone in this town, forget everything I have done for this family over the last forty years. I mean, I raised those children when my husband was working double shifts at the plant, I kept that house spotless, and now... now they use the church, the one place I thought was safe, to orchestrate this... this campaign against me. It's just so overwhelming when you realize the people you broke bread with are conspiring against you on such a grand scale.
Do you have any proof that your in-laws are actually using the church to plot against you?

Proof? Well, doctor, if you're asking for a signed document or a tape recording, no, I don't have that. But you don't need a piece of paper when the signs are literally right in front of your face. Like I said, I came in because I knew my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. I mean, arguing is one thing—arguing is when Mary-Beth says my pot roast is dry, which it isn't, by the way. I slow-cook it for six hours. But this... this is so much bigger. 

I saw it plain as day in the church bulletin last Sunday. There was a special announcement about the parish committee restructuring, and right there, right next to the altar flower donations—which I used to organize, mind you, for over a decade—was my sister-in-law's name in bold print. And who was listed right below her? Her son, my nephew. They are using the altar, the literal altar of the Lord, and the parish committee to completely push me out. 

It’s all connected. If you look at how they arranged the seating for the upcoming jubilee, they’ve put me all the way in the back, near the vestibule doors. Why would they do that? To make everyone forget what I have done for this family! They want the congregation to look up at the front pews and see only them, as if I never existed, as if I didn't organize every single bake sale from 1985 to 2002. They want to erase my legacy, doctor. They want to rewrite the history of our family in that church, and they are using the committee meetings—which they suddenly moved to Tuesday nights, knowing full well I have my arthritis water aerobics on Tuesdays—to do it. So, proof? The proof is in the orchestration of it all. You just have to know how to read between the lines, and I finally see it all perfectly clearly.
Do you think it's possible that your in-laws are not actually plotting against you?

Possible? Oh, doctor, you sound just like Pastor Dave when I tried to explain it to him after service. He said, 'Now, Helen, maybe it's just a coincidence.' A coincidence! No, no, it's not possible. I mean, you really have to look at the whole picture, the entire tapestry of what's been happening over the last few months. It's not just a feeling I have, it's a knowing. I came in here today because I *knew*, I absolutely knew without a shadow of a doubt, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. Arguing is normal. Arguing is what families do over the holidays. But this... they are using the altar, the sacred altar of our church, and the entire parish committee to push me out completely. 

It’s not possible that I’m wrong because the pieces fit together too perfectly. Why else would they change the committee meeting times? Why else would my sister-in-law suddenly take over the flower arrangements—something she has never shown an ounce of interest in before? She doesn't even know the difference between a peony and a ranunculus! It’s all calculated to make everyone in that congregation forget what I have done for this family and that church. They want to erase me, doctor. They want to wipe my slate clean so they can stand up there at the altar and look like the pillars of the community, while I’m shoved in the back by the vestibule doors like some forgotten relic. So, no, I don't think it's possible that they aren't plotting against me. I see it as clearly as I see you sitting there. It's all just so overwhelmingly obvious once you open your eyes to it.
How long have you thought your in-laws were plotting against you?

Well, doctor, if I really sit back and think about the exact timeline of it all... it's been about two months now. Yes, two months exactly. It all started around the beginning of November. You see, we have this tradition, or well, I started the tradition, of setting up a Día de los Muertos altar at the house. My late husband’s grandmother was from Mexico, and even though I’m not, I always felt it was so important to honor that side of the family’s heritage. I would spend weeks gathering the marigolds, baking the pan de muerto from scratch—which is not easy, let me tell you, getting the yeast to rise just right in this autumn weather—and setting out all the photos. 

And then, about two months ago, right before the celebration, we had this massive, blowout fight. My sister-in-law had the nerve to tell me I was doing it all wrong, that the sugar skulls were too gaudy, and that I was making a spectacle of their family history. A spectacle! After all the love and care I put into it! That was the turning point, doctor. That fight over the Día de los Muertos altar was when the veil was lifted. That’s when I realized this wasn't just typical family bickering anymore. That’s when the plotting started, or at least when I finally noticed it. Ever since that day, for these past two months, it’s been one thing after another, escalating into this whole crisis with the church bulletin and the parish committee. Two months of absolute torment, doctor, watching them try to systematically dismantle everything I am.
Do you believe that the church bulletin or the parish committee's actions are specifically about you or directed at you in a way that's unique to your situation?

Oh, absolutely. It is entirely about me. There’s no other explanation, doctor. I mean, why else would they do it? It’s not like they care about the church bulletin or the committee itself. They don't! My sister-in-law hasn't volunteered for a single bake sale in fifteen years, and now suddenly she’s practically running the parish committee? No, it’s all directed right at me. 

Like I told you, I came in here because I finally realized, I *knew* deep down, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. This isn't just about a disagreement over a pot roast or the Día de los Muertos altar. They are using the altar—the actual, physical altar of the church—and the parish committee as weapons. They are using them to push me out completely. It’s a very specific, targeted campaign to make everyone in that congregation forget what I have done for this family. They know how much the church means to me, how much time I’ve dedicated to it. They know that if they can take that away from me, if they can erase my legacy there, then they win. So yes, every single action they take, every meeting they reschedule, every name they print in bold in that bulletin... it is uniquely, specifically, and maliciously directed at me.
Do you think there's anything that could happen, or any information you could receive, that would make you question or change your belief about your in-laws plotting against you?

Change my mind? Well... no. No, doctor, I don't see how that could ever happen. Because, you see, it's not a theory. It's not a guess that I've just come up with out of thin air. When you know something, when you feel it in your bones and see the evidence of it every single day, there's no going back from that. 

I mean, what could they possibly show me? A letter from my sister-in-law saying she loves me? I wouldn't believe it for a second. It would just be another trick, another layer to the deception. Because, like I said before, I came in here today because the truth finally hit me. I *knew*, with absolute certainty, that they weren't just arguing with me anymore. This isn't about some petty disagreement. They are using the altar—our sacred altar—and the entire parish committee to push me out completely. They are systematically working to make everyone in that congregation forget what I have done for this family and for that church. 

So, no, there isn't a single piece of information, not a single document or conversation, that could change my mind. When you've seen the strings being pulled, when you've watched them try to erase your entire legacy right in front of your eyes... well, you can't just un-see that, can you? You can't just pretend it's not happening when it's the absolute truth.
Do you think there are other people outside of your family and church who are also plotting against you?

Well, outside the family and the church... I mean, if you really stop and think about it, doctor, it's a very good question. Because once you see how deep the rot goes, you have to wonder who else they've gotten to, right? But... no, I haven't seen the mailman acting strange, or the cashier at the grocery store, if that's what you mean. The woman at the bakery still gives me a smile when I buy my rolls on Tuesdays. 

But you have to understand, they don't *need* the whole town to be in on it. They don't need the outside world. Why would they bother? They have the two things that matter most to me. Like I've been trying to explain, and I really hope you're grasping the gravity of this... I came in here to see you because I finally *knew*, without a shadow of a doubt, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. This wasn't just bickering. They are actively, maliciously using the altar and the parish committee to push me out completely. That's their domain. That's where they hold the power right now. They are using those sacred things to make absolutely everyone in that congregation forget what I have done for this family. They want to erase my entire legacy, my contributions, everything I've built and nurtured. So they don't need outsiders plotting against me. They are doing a perfectly thorough job of destroying my life from the inside out, using the very people and places I loved the most. It's so calculated, doctor, so incredibly cruel... they've contained their plotting to the places that will hurt me the most.
Do you believe that events or actions unrelated to your family or church, such as something you see on the news or a stranger's behavior, are somehow connected to the plot against you?

Well, the news... no, I wouldn't say the news anchor is talking to me, or that a stranger crossing the street is in on it. I mean, I watch the local news every evening at six, just like I have for thirty years, and it's just the weather and the traffic and whatever nonsense is happening downtown. They aren't talking about me. And the people at the grocery store, the strangers, they're just buying their milk and going home. 

But you see, doctor, that's exactly what makes what's happening so incredibly insidious. It's not some grand, crazy conspiracy involving the whole world. It's intimate. It's personal. And that's why it hurts so much, and why I had to come in here and talk to you. Because it's not the strangers I have to worry about. Like I've been saying, and I really need you to understand the depth of this... I came in because I finally *knew*, I saw it with crystal clarity, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. This wasn't about who hosts Thanksgiving or who brings the potato salad. They are using the altar—the very heart of our church—and the parish committee to push me out completely. They are manipulating the very fabric of our community to make absolutely everyone forget what I have done for this family. All my sacrifices, all the years I spent building us up... they want it erased. So, no, the strangers on the street aren't involved. My in-laws don't need them. They are doing enough damage all on their own, right where I live and breathe.
Do you think that things you see or hear in your daily life, like on TV or in conversations with strangers, are somehow related to your in-laws' plot against you?

Doctor, I feel like we are going in circles here, I really do. Like I was just saying a moment ago, the television is just the television. When I turn on my shows, or watch the game shows in the afternoon, they're just playing their games. The people at the bus stop are just waiting for the bus. They aren't whispering about me. I don't know why you keep asking about strangers and the TV, because that's not the problem at all! 

The problem—and I feel like I have to keep repeating this so you can truly understand the sheer weight of what is happening to me—is my family. I came in here to see you, specifically, because it finally hit me, just like a bolt of lightning, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. We used to bicker, sure, every family bickers about little things. But this? This is entirely different. They are literally using the altar—the sacred altar at our church, where my own children were baptized, where I've arranged the Easter lilies for twenty-two years—and they are using the parish committee to push me out completely. 

They are manipulating the very foundation of our church, the place I have devoted my life to, just to make everyone, every single person in that congregation, forget what I have done for this family. They want to wipe my slate clean, erase my history, make me a ghost in my own life so they can take all the credit. So no, I'm not worried about the TV. I'm not worried about a conversation with a stranger at the market. It's them. It's always been them, doctor. And they are using the church to do it, which is the most unforgivable part of it all.
Is there anything, no matter how small, that could make you slightly doubt your belief that your in-laws are plotting against you?

Doubt it? Doctor, how could I possibly doubt it? I mean, really, if you were in my shoes, if you had lived the life I’ve lived and seen the things I’ve seen, you wouldn’t doubt it for a second. It’s not something you can just brush off or second-guess, like... like misplacing your keys or wondering if you left the stove on. This isn't a feeling. It's a fact. 

I know you have to ask these questions, I understand that’s your job, but you really have to listen to what I’m telling you. The proof is right there in front of me, every single Sunday, every single committee meeting. I didn't come in here because I had a passing suspicion or a bad dream. I came in because I *knew*, with absolute, terrifying certainty, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. We've had our spats over the years—who hasn't?—but this has escalated into a full-blown campaign to destroy me. 

There is no room for doubt when they are literally using the altar of our church, the most sacred space we have, and the parish committee to push me out completely. I see the way they look at me during the passing of the peace. I see the way they maneuver the conversations at the coffee hour. They are systematically working to make everyone, every single person in that congregation, forget what I have done for this family. All the bake sales I organized, the Sunday school classes I taught, the times I held this family together when my husband's brother was drinking... they want all of that erased. They want me gone. So, no, doctor. There isn't a single thing, not a shred of evidence or a tiny little inkling, that could make me doubt it. It is happening, and it is destroying my life.
Is there anything that could happen or any information you could receive that would make you completely change your mind about your in-laws plotting against you?

Doctor, please. I... I really don't understand why you're asking me the exact same thing again. Are you waiting for a different answer? Because the truth doesn't change just because you rephrase the question. What could possibly happen to change my mind? An apology from them? A confession? Even if they stood up right there at the pulpit on Sunday morning and confessed to the whole congregation, it wouldn't change the fact that they've already set the wheels in motion! 

I feel like a broken record, and I'm sorry to keep repeating myself, but I have to make you understand why I am sitting in this chair today. I came in because I knew—not guessed, not suspected, but absolutely *knew* in my bones—that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. We are way, way past normal family bickering over burnt roasts or whose turn it is to buy the Christmas gifts. They are actively using the altar, the very center of our faith, and the parish committee to push me out. To completely push me out of the picture and isolate me from the only community I have left. 

And why are they doing it? To make everyone forget what I have done for this family. All the years I kept the peace, all the holidays I hosted, all the times I bit my tongue and smiled when they were nothing but cruel... they want it all gone, wiped from everyone's memory. So no, there is no piece of information, no magic wand you can wave, no secret document you can show me that would make me change my mind. How can I change my mind about something I am living through every single day? You can't un-see something once your eyes are open to it. They are doing this to me. And instead of asking me what it would take to make me stop believing the truth, you should be asking me how on earth I am supposed to survive it!
Is there any small part of you that sometimes wonders if you might be misinterpreting your in-laws' actions?

Doctor, I... I am starting to feel very frustrated, to be perfectly honest with you. We are going over and over the same ground, and you keep asking me if I'm mistaken, if I'm misinterpreting, if I'm doubting... and it's like you aren't hearing the words coming out of my mouth! 

I don't know how else to explain this so that it finally clicks for you. There is no "small part of me" that wonders anything, because there is nothing to wonder about. I am a sixty-year-old woman, I have raised a family, I have lived a full life, and I know the difference between a misunderstanding and a deliberate, calculated attack. 

Like I have said—and I feel like I am just echoing myself in this room—I came in here because I knew, without a shadow of a doubt, that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. This isn't about me taking something the wrong way when they didn't invite me to Sunday dinner, or me reading too much into a sideways glance at the grocery store. I wish it were that simple! I really do. But it's not. 

They are using the altar. They are using the parish committee. The very people I have served alongside for over two decades! They are using them to push me out, completely and utterly, and to make everyone in our community forget what I have done for this family. To erase me. How do you misinterpret that, Doctor? How do you look at a coordinated effort to destroy your standing in your own church and say, "Oh, maybe I'm just looking at this wrong?" You don't. You see it for exactly what it is. And that is exactly what I am doing.
Do you think your in-laws' actions against you are part of a larger, more complex plot involving other people or organizations outside of your family and church?

Well, you see... that's the thing about all of this, Doctor. It’s like pulling a thread on a sweater, isn't it? You pull one little piece, and suddenly the whole thing starts unraveling, and you see how everything is connected. I’ve spent a lot of time thinking about this, lying awake at night just turning it over and over in my head, because it doesn't just stop at the church doors. It can't. 

I mean, I came in here today, like I’ve been trying to tell you, because I knew—I absolutely knew—that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. This isn't just family bickering. They are using the altar, the most sacred place in our lives, and the parish committee to push me out completely and make everyone forget what I have done for this family. But how could they do that alone? How could my sister-in-law, who can barely organize a potluck without my help, suddenly orchestrate this massive campaign to erase me from the community? 

She can’t. They can’t. They must have help. I’ve noticed the mail carrier looking at me differently when he drops off the letters, lingering just a second too long at the edge of the driveway. And the women at the bank—the tellers I’ve gone to for twenty years—they whisper now when I walk in. They whisper, and they look down at their screens like they’re checking some... some file on me. It’s obvious that my in-laws have reached out to them. They’ve probably contacted the local businesses, maybe even the town council, spreading these lies to make sure that everywhere I go, people are turning their backs on me. 

It’s a whole network, Doctor. It has to be. Because you don't just use the parish committee to destroy a person's life without making sure the rest of the town is in on it too. They want me completely isolated, completely cut off, so that when they finally push me out for good, there won't be a single person left to stand up and say, "Wait, remember what she did for that family?" They’ve thought of everything, and they’ve got everyone involved. It’s... it’s just so much bigger than a family feud. It’s a complete takeover of my life.
Is there anything that could make you reconsider your beliefs about your in-laws' actions, no matter how small it might seem?

Doctor, respectfully, I... I just don't understand why we keep going over the exact same ground. Are you trying to wear me down? Because I feel like you're just waiting for me to suddenly crack and say, 'Oh, you're right, silly me, I just misunderstood!' But I can't do that. I can't reconsider because there is nothing to reconsider. 

I mean, really think about what you're asking me. You're asking me to doubt my own waking life. I have told you exactly why I am sitting in this room. I came in because I knew—not guessed, not wondered, but absolutely knew—that my in-laws were not just arguing with me anymore. If this was just a normal family spat about... about who brings the potato salad to the summer reunion or who said what at Thanksgiving, I would have handled it. I always handle it! I'm the one who always smoothed things over. 

But they took it so much further than that. They are using the altar. The altar of our church! And they are using the parish committee to push me out, to completely exile me from my own community, and to make everyone forget what I have done for this family. All my sacrifices, all the years I held everything together when things were hard, all the love I poured into them... they just want it gone. They want to erase my entire legacy. 

So when you ask if there's some tiny little thing, some minor detail that would make me change my mind... it honestly feels a bit insulting, Doctor. It's like you're asking me to reconsider if the sky is up. I am living this nightmare every single day, watching them actively dismantle my life and my reputation piece by piece. There is no reconsidering. There is only the truth of what they are doing to me, and I just have to find a way to live through it.
Do you think that events or actions unrelated to your family or church are somehow connected to you or have a special meaning for you?

Well, see, that's just it, Doctor. You say 'unrelated,' but... well, what is really unrelated anymore? I know I keep beating this same drum, and I know I've told you this already, but it's the absolute center of everything happening to me right now, so I have to keep bringing it up. 

I didn't walk into this clinic today because I'm just looking at random things happening in the world and thinking they're about me. I don't think the evening news anchor is sending me secret messages, if that's the sort of thing you're getting at. I am here because of a very real, very specific nightmare that is happening to me. Like I keep saying, this is about my in-laws. That is the root of it all. I came in because I finally realized they weren't just having a typical family argument with me. They took this to the altar. They took it to the parish committee! They are using the very church I love to push me out completely and make every single person in our lives forget everything I've done for this family over the last forty years. 

So when you ask about other events... well, if a neighbor suddenly puts up a new privacy fence, or if the local paper runs a story about community restructuring... it might look completely unrelated to you. You might just see a fence or a newspaper. But to me? I have to sit there and wonder, is this just another piece of their plan? Is this another way they are trying to box me out? Did they talk to the neighbor? Because when your own family uses your sacred spaces to systematically destroy your reputation and erase your legacy, nothing feels unrelated anymore. Every little thing that happens in this town just feels like another ripple from what they started at that church. It all just circles right back to them and what they are doing to get rid of me.
Is there anything, no matter how small, that could make you question the plot against you, even if just for a moment?

Doctor, I... I feel like we are just spinning our wheels here. Didn't you just ask me this exact same thing? I’m starting to feel like a broken record, and I don't mean to be difficult, I really don't, but I just don't know how else to explain this to you so that it sinks in. Are you waiting for me to slip up and change my story? Because the story doesn't change when it's the truth. 

I have to say it again, because maybe my words just aren't capturing the reality of it for you. I came in here today because I knew—with absolute, undeniable certainty—that my in-laws were not just arguing with me. If it were just bickering over holiday plans or who said what to whom, I wouldn't be sitting in this chair. But they are using the altar... the literal, sacred altar of our church! And they are using the parish committee to systematically push me out and make everyone forget what I have done for this family. 

How on earth could I question that, even for a moment, when I see it happening right in front of my face? I spent forty years—forty years, Doctor!—making sure my husband's family looked respectable. I organized the funeral luncheons, I baked for every single charity drive, I held the family together through thick and thin. I poured my blood, sweat, and tears into that church and that family. And now, my sister-in-law stands up there near the communion line, whispering to the committee members, plotting to just erase my entire existence from the community. 

So, no. No, I don't question it. Not for a single second. Because questioning it would mean I'm crazy, or blind, or that I don't know my own life. And I do know my life. I know exactly what they are doing. They are using the church to get rid of me. I just... I really don't understand why you keep asking me if I doubt it. Why would I doubt my own eyes?
Is there anything at all that could ever make you think that your in-laws are not plotting against you?

Doctor, I... I just have to ask, are you actually listening to a single word I am saying to you? Because I feel like I am talking to a brick wall here. We have literally just gone over this, and over this, and over this. No. The answer is no. There is absolutely nothing in this world that could make me think they aren't doing this, because they are doing this. I didn't just wake up one morning and decide to come to a clinic for my health. 

I have told you, I came in because I knew—and I mean I knew it in my bones, as sure as I am breathing the air in this room—that my in-laws were not just having some petty family argument with me. If it was just a normal argument, I wouldn't be sitting here! I would be at home, baking a pie and smoothing it over like I always do. But they took it to the altar. The altar of our church! And they are actively using the parish committee to push me out, to completely exile me, and to make everyone in that congregation forget every single thing I have done for this family. 

I spent decades building us up, decades of Sunday schools and potlucks and keeping the peace, and they are tearing it down right in front of the whole parish. So why... why do you keep asking me if I can just pretend it's not happening? I can't pretend! I can't just wave a magic wand and say, oh, maybe they aren't plotting against me, when they are using the church committee to literally erase my entire life's work. I just... I need you to actually hear what I am saying to you instead of asking me the exact same question four different ways. Can you please just acknowledge what they are doing to me?
Do you think your in-laws would actually be capable of organizing such a complex plot against you without anyone else noticing?

Doctor, I... honestly, I don't know if you're trying to trip me up or if you just don't understand the kind of people we're dealing with here. Capable? Of course they're capable! You don't know my sister-in-law, Martha. She has been on the parish council for fifteen years, she knows every single person who volunteers for the flower guild, she organizes the usher schedule... she has her fingers in absolutely everything. So when you ask if they could organize something like this without anyone noticing... well, that's just the thing, people *are* noticing, but they're too afraid to say anything, or they've already been brainwashed by her! 

It’s not just some random plot, it’s a systematic dismantling of my life, and yes, they are completely capable of it. I keep telling you, I came in here today, I made this appointment, because I finally saw it clearly. I knew—I just knew it deep down in my soul—that they were not just arguing with me anymore. This isn't just about who hosts Thanksgiving or some petty squabble over a casserole dish. They are using the altar. The actual altar of the church! And they are using the parish committee, using their influence, to push me out completely. 

They want to make everyone in that congregation, people I have known for forty years, forget everything I have done for this family. All the bake sales, all the support, the thousands of hours I gave to make them look good... they are trying to erase it all. And they are doing it right there during coffee hour, whispering to the committee, turning everyone against me. So yes, they are capable. They are more than capable, they are doing it right now as we speak! I just... I don't understand why you can't see how serious this is.
Do you think the plot against you is limited to your in-laws or if other people or organizations are also involved?

Doctor, I... honestly, it's like a web, isn't it? It starts with one thread and then it just spreads and spreads until you're completely tangled up in it. So, when you ask if it's just my in-laws... well, of course it starts with them. Martha and her little clique, my brother-in-law Tom who just nods along with whatever she says... but it doesn't stop there. How could it? They don't have the power to do this all on their own without pulling the strings of the people around them. 

I mean, I've told you this, I keep telling you why I finally had to come in here and talk to someone. I came in because I knew—and I mean, I saw the writing on the wall so clearly it was blinding—that my in-laws were not just arguing with me over some silly family nonsense. It wasn't about me being too overbearing or whatever they like to claim. No, they were using the altar. The altar! The very heart of our church! And they are using the parish committee to do their dirty work. 

So, yes, the committee is involved now. They have to be. Martha whispers in the ear of the head of the finance committee, she nods at the choir director during the peace offering... they are all in on it now. They are all working together to push me out, to completely isolate me from the community I helped build. They want to make everyone—every single person who sits in those pews on Sunday—forget what I have done for this family. All the sacrifices, all the hours I put in to make sure we were respected and loved... they want it all erased. And they are using the entire parish structure to do it. It's not just Martha anymore, Doctor. It's the whole church. They've turned the House of God into a weapon against me, and I just... I don't know how to fight an entire congregation.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?
